The conquest also involved the destruction of Inca cultural systems, such as their advanced farming methods known as the vertical archipelago model of agriculture [1]. Furthermore, the Spanish implemented the Inca mita corvée labor system for colonial purposes, often forcing Inca families to work in gold and silver mines, particularly the massive silver mine at Potosí [1].
